p0_findings.finding: business_members carries an ALL policy (business_members_manage_owner_manager) whose USING/WITH CHECK validate only the ACTOR (active owner OR MANAGER of the business), never the row being written, while authenticated holds full DML on the table. Per catalog reads at 2026-08-06, an active MANAGER can insert/update/delete any membership row in their business directly from an authenticated browser client - self-promotion to owner, removal of owners - bypassing the named-command architecture and making the registry-required last-owner protection unenforceable at the data layer.
p0_findings.evidence: pg_policy + has_table_privilege + pg_get_functiondef reads on production (execute_sql, read-only); app_is_business_member/app_is_admin are SECURITY DEFINER so no 42P17 recursion barrier protects the path
p0_findings.runtime_confirmation: deliberately NOT run against production (no exploit against real data); to be reproduced and measured on the disposable stack in the ACP-021 harness
p0_findings.proposed_fix: owner-gated hardening migration: drop or row-constrain the ALL policy (named server commands are the sanctioned mutation path) and revoke authenticated/anon DML on business_members; must be reviewed before apply

p0_findings.finding: business_accounts_update_owner_manager policy contains a correlation bug: its EXISTS compares bm.business_account_id = bm.id (the membership row's own two uuid columns, effectively never equal) instead of correlating to business_accounts.id - so the policy silently reduces to app_is_admin() and owners/managers cannot update their business row through the RLS path.
p0_findings.proposed_fix: same owner-gated hardening migration; MER-014 settings writes go through service_role named commands and are unaffected

p0_findings.severity: P2 (PII exposure in a merchant-facing URL; FIXED before any deploy, never reached production)
p0_findings.finding: The MER-008 customer list rendered the internal grouping key (phone:5405550142) inside every customer link, placing a real recipient phone number in the page HTML, the address bar, browser history, referrer headers and any path-logging middleware. The registry forbids unnecessary PII in list view.
p0_findings.evidence: e2e/disposable/customerBook.mjs check C3 against rendered HTML on the first run; the code had been read twice without the leak being noticed
p0_findings.status: FIXED at cd697e4 before the screen was ever promoted or deployed. The browser now receives publicCustomerKey: a sha-256 digest salted with the business account id, truncated to 32 hex, computed server-side only. C5b asserts links carry an opaque key.
p0_findings.lesson: The masking was correct in the projection and wrong in the URL. Asserting on rendered HTML rather than on a component prop is what separated those.
